Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 60, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Mumtahanah (the One Who Is Examined), because it mentions the verse about the examination of the women emigrants (muhajirat) who came from Makkah to Madinah.

From the Aims of the Surah

• A warning to the believers against allying themselves with the enemies, and an alert that their enemies seize the opportunity to harm them; and that the ties of kinship between them and the polytheists carry no weight in the face of enmity over religion.

• The obligation to examine the believing women who come as emigrants, the explanation of what follows from that examination if their faith is established, the ruling on giving the pledge (bay'ah) to emigrant believing women, and the conditions of this pledge.

[Tafsir]

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not take My enemy and your enemy as close friends and allies, conveying affection to them, informing them of the news of the Messenger ﷺ and the secrets of the Muslims, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, namely faith in Allah and His Messenger and what was revealed to him of the Qur'an. They expel the Messenger and expel you, O believers, from "Makkah," because you believe in Allah, your Lord, and affirm His oneness. If you, O believers, have emigrated striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure, then do not ally with My enemies and your enemies, conveying affection to them secretly. I know best what you conceal and what you reveal. Whoever among you does this has certainly strayed from the path of truth and right, and has gone astray from the straight way.

If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you, and they will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with killing and captivity, and with insult and abuse. And they have wished, in every circumstance, that you would disbelieve just as they do.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 60, verse 3:

Your relatives and your children will not benefit you at all on the Day of Resurrection, when you take the disbelievers as allies for their sake. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will separate you: He will admit the people of His obedience into Paradise and the people of disobedience into the Fire. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do; nothing of your words or your deeds is hidden from Him.

Indeed there has been for you (O believers) an excellent example in Ibrahim (Abraham) (peace be upon him) and those who were with him among the believers, when they said to their disbelieving people: "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah, of the deities and rivals. We have rejected you, and we have denounced the disbelief you are upon. Enmity and hatred have become manifest between us and you forever, as long as you remain upon your disbelief, until you believe in Allah alone." However, the seeking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father is not included in the emulation, for that occurred only before it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of Allah. So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. ﴿Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the final return﴾ [60:4].

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 60, verse 5:

"Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise."

Meaning: "Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers, by punishing us at their hands, or by empowering the disbelievers over us, so that they tempt us away from our religion, or prevail over us and are themselves tried by that, saying, 'If these people were upon the truth, this punishment would not have befallen them,' and so they increase in disbelief. And cover over our sins for us by Your pardon of them, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Mighty, who cannot be overcome, the Wise in His sayings and His actions."

For you, O believers, there was indeed a good example in Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him, and those who were with him, for whoever hopes for good from Allah in this world and the Hereafter. As for whoever turns away from what Allah has urged him to, namely following His prophets, and takes as allies the enemies of Allah, then indeed Allah is Ghani (Self-Sufficient), free of need from His servants, Hamid (Praiseworthy) in His essence and His attributes, praised in every circumstance.

It may be that Allah will place between you, O believers, and between those among your relatives whom you have opposed, who are polytheists, affection after hatred and harmony after animosity, through the opening of their hearts to Islam. Allah is capable of everything. Allah is Most Forgiving toward His servants and Most Merciful to them.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 60, verse 8:

Allah does not forbid you, O believers, from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being kind to them and dealing justly with them, by doing good to them and showing them kindness. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly in their words and their deeds.

Allah only forbids you from those who fought you because of your religion, expelled you from your homes, and helped others to expel you, from making them your allies by giving them support and affection. Whoever takes them as helpers against the believers and as close friends, those are the wrongdoers against themselves, who have transgressed the limits of Allah.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and act by His law! When believing women come to you as emigrants from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam, then test them, so that you may know the truth of their faith. Allah knows best the reality of their faith. If you know them to be believers according to what appears to you of the signs and evidences, then do not return them to their disbelieving husbands. For believing women are not lawful for them (the disbelievers), and disbelievers are not lawful for believing women. Give their husbands what they spent on them as dowries. There is no sin upon you in marrying them once you have given them their dowries. Do not hold on to marriage with your disbelieving wives. Ask the polytheists for what you spent as dowries for your wives who apostatized from Islam and joined them, and let them ask for what they spent as dowries for their Muslim wives who embraced Islam and joined you. That is the ruling mentioned in the verse; it is the judgment of Allah, by which He judges among you, so do not oppose it. And Allah is All-Knowing, nothing is hidden from Him, and All-Wise in His sayings and actions.

And if some of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and the disbelievers have not returned the dowries (mahr, the marriage gift) that you paid to them, then if you later gain victory over those disbelievers or others and prevail against them, give to the Muslim men whose wives have gone the equivalent of the dowries they paid, from the spoils of war or from other wealth. And fear Allah, in whom you believe.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 60, verse 12:

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَاءَكَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ يُبَايِعْنَكَ عَلَىٰ أَن لَّا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَسْرِقْنَ وَلَا يَزْنِينَ وَلَا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ وَلَا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتَانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ وَلَا يَعْصِينَكَ فِي مَعْرُوفٍ فَبَايِعْهُنَّ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾
